title: Regioned processing exceptions & KMS safeguards - Lockridge Capital
summary: Lockridge wants firm-level EU-only processing for most data but needs a small set of cross-border exceptions (fraud detection + payment clearing). The call focused on how Redwood can support regioned processing with explicit exception workflows, KMS separation (BYOK + per-region keys), audit log retention, and a subprocessor carve-out process. Action items: deliver SOC2 artifacts, detailed subprocessor matrix, and an architecture diagram for KMS segmentation and exception routing.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-09
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Avery Cho (Redwood AE), Miguel Santos (Redwood SE), Sana Rafiq (CISO, Lockridge), Tom Breyer (Head of Platform), Leah Kim (Legal), Arjun Patel (SRE)
Shared links: Redwood security overview (https://redwood.example.com/security.pdf), subprocessor spreadsheet (link: /shared/lockridge-subprocessors.csv), KMS diagram (to be shared)

[00:00] Avery (Redwood): hey everyone good to see you all thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:07] Sana (Lockridge): hi yea thanks, Sana here CISO.
[00:10] Tom (Lockridge): Tom, platform.
[00:12] Leah (Lockridge): Leah, legal.
[00:14] Arjun (Lockridge): Arjun, SRE.
[00:16] Miguel (Redwood): Miguel, solutions engineering. great to meet you.

[00:30] Avery: high level: i know you asked for EU-only processing for customer PII, but you also mentioned a small bucket of traffic that needs to cross to the US for payment clearing and fraud scoring; want to confirm that scope before we dive in.
[00:45] Sana: correct. most user data must remain in eu- region, no cross border. exceptions: payment processors and a fraud model that runs in us today. Ideally those exceptions are explicitly minimised and audited.
[01:05] Miguel: ok sounds good. a couple of ways we typically support this: 1) region-affinity routing with strict processing policies, 2) explicit exception routes where payloads are tagged and routed to a different policy, and 3) data minimization transforms pre-routing - e.g., tokenization or hashed identifiers before cross-border call.
[01:30] Arjun: can you do tokenization on the edge, so the us service never sees PII? we'd prefer that to be honest; don't want raw emails or ssns moving.
[01:42] Miguel: yes, you can push an extraction step to the platform or client that redacts fields. we also support policy-level redaction but that is server-side and in your eu cluster by default. for exceptions we can route only the minimal fields out. sometimes the transcription shows K B cache but i mean KV cache, sorry the auto-output.

[02:05] Leah: from a legal perspective we need an auditable exception flow: who approved each cross-border record, retention windows, and access controls. can redwood provide an approval workflow or at least logs we can export?
[02:20] Avery: absolutely. we have audit logs that capture request metadata, model variant, route decision, and decision reason. logs are streamed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder or can be S3-delivered. retention configurable per-customer but default is 90 days.
[02:38] Sana: 90 days might be low for us; we need 2 years for certain financial records. is that configurable?
[02:45] Miguel: yes configurable. we can push to long-term archive (encrypted S3) with customer-managed lifecycle and lifecycle rules. access is RBAC-controlled.

[03:05] Tom: about keys — we're leaning to BYOK, we want separate keys for EU and US processing so that if data crosses, it remains under different key domains. can you do per-region KMS segregation?
[03:20] Miguel: yes. options: 1) Redwood-managed keys with per-region key realms (not BYOK), 2) BYOK where you upload keys per region (we support cloud KMS like AWS KMS/CloudHSM, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault), or 3) split-key escrow where you keep a part of the key. for strict separation we recommend BYOK per-region and separate key policies. note there is operational overhead for rotation and key pinging.
[03:55] Arjun: would BYOK require network connectivity to your control plane? we operate in a VPC.
[04:02] Miguel: if you go private deployment (VPC), KMS traffic stays inside your network — Redwood's private control plane can proxy key ops without keys leaving your VPC. for hosted mode with BYOK we request a wrapped key and we use an HSM-backed environment but the wrapped key is not unwrapped without customer authorization. small mis-transcribe earlier said K S as K S, but it's K M S for key management service.

[04:40] Leah: what's the model for subprocessors? we need to know who touches data, and have a notice window if you add a new subprocessor.
[04:50] Avery: our standard is a subprocessor list updated monthly; for enterprise we support a 30-60 day notification window and a carve-out where Lockridge can require a non-critical fallback if a subprocessor is unacceptable. we'll supply the current inventory (see shared sheet).
[05:05] Sana: do you have any eu-located subprocessors that store or process data outside eu? specifically, model hosting or inference is a concern.
[05:16] Miguel: the hosted API generally routes to region-specific clusters — eu clusters in frankfurt or dublin depending on availability. we do replicate to us for disaster recovery but for eu-only baseline we can disable cross-region replication and pin to euro clusters. exceptions still possible via explicit exception routes.

[05:45] Tom: how is routing enforced? is it a config in console or an API?
[05:50] Avery: both. we can give you a policy-as-code spec that maps routes to regions and reason codes. you can push policies via API and we can enforce at the edge via request headers or token scopes.

[06:10] Arjun: audit trail: do logs include who approved an exception and the original payload? we want redaction but traceability.
[06:20] Miguel: logs include request id, route decision, approver id (if approval flow used), and a hashed payload reference. payloads can be archived encrypted with your KMS and only retrievable with multi-party approval. note: retrieval process may be manual depending on your workflow.

[06:45] Leah: on SOC2 and ISO evidence — can you provide the latest SOC2 Type II and your ISO27001 certificates? also pen test results?
[06:55] Avery: yes. we'll share the SOC2 report and ISO attestation under NDA. pen test summary and mitigation roadmap too. sending after the call.

[07:10] Sana: another ask: how do you handle caching? CV cache? (meaning KV cache) specifically we don't want caches to be replicated cross-border.
[07:20] Miguel: good catch — KV cache placement is per-cluster. caches in the eu cluster stay in eu. we can also scope prefix caching so that any data marked as "eu-only" is kept out of cross-region caches.

[07:40] Tom: latency concerns — if we route exceptions to us, what's typical added latency?
[07:45] Miguel: added latency will be network and extra hops; from frankfurt to us-east we estimate 60-120ms additional RTT, tokenization/transform steps add another ~10-40ms depending on batch. we can run a quick benchmark in the pilot.

[08:10] Arjun: can we do canary rules so a small percentage of traffic hits exception path to test?
[08:15] Avery: yes canary and A/B controls are supported in console; you can limit by route, user bucket, or header.

[08:30] Leah: what about legal hold? we may need to place a subset of records on litigation hold longer than normal retention.
[08:38] Miguel: we support per-request retention overrides flagged into lifecycle. these go to long-term archive and require an RBAC role to release.

[08:55] Sana: question about SSO and RBAC mapping — our IdP is Okta. we want to ensure least privilege and segmented admin roles between eu-only ops and cross-border approvers.
[09:05] Avery: SSO via SAML/OIDC with group mapping. you can define roles like 'eu-admin' and 'exceptions-approver' and map them to Okta groups. we also support SCIM for automated provisioning.

[09:25] Tom: are audit logs tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody in case of compliance audits.
[09:30] Miguel: logs are write-once via append-only storage with integrity checks and checksums; we can provide signed log packages on request.

[09:45] Leah: escape hatch question: if a subprocessor is added that we can't accept, what's the remediation?
[09:52] Avery: we'll honor the enterprise clause: you can require us to stop sending traffic to that subprocessor and we'll provide a fallback model variant or private node until resolution.

[10:05] Sana: for the KMS flow — if we provide BYOK keys per region, do you rotate them? do we keep rotation control?
[10:15] Miguel: rotation is configurable. you can control rotation schedules in your KMS; Redwood will accept rotated wrapped keys. we recommend you manage key rotation and we can coordinate rotation windows via API.

[10:35] Arjun: a technical nit: when an exception is triggered, how do you ensure the exception payload doesn't accidentally include PII fields beyond what's approved? we need field-level allowlist/denylist.
[10:45] Miguel: we support field-level schemas and validation rules. requests that violate schema are rejected with a decision code. you can also run a pre-send transform plug-in in your VPC that enforces allow-lists.

[11:10] Leah: liability: does Redwood take responsibility for subprocessors? we need contractual language and DPA clauses.
[11:18] Avery: yes our enterprise DPA includes subprocessor commitments, notification windows and indemnity clauses; legal can exchange redlines.

[11:35] Miguel: some operational notes — for pilot we'd propose: a) deploy region-affinity policy in staging, b) run a small canary (1-5%) of traffic through exception with hashed payloads, c) measure latency and audit log fidelity, d) validate KMS wrapping/unwrapping flow.

[12:00] Tom: timeline — we want a 6-week pilot, then production gated on legal sign-off. any blockers?
[12:08] Avery: sounds fine. we'll need an NDA for SOC2, and Lockridge needs to provide Okta test creds and a contact for KMS side.

[12:25] Sana: what about subprocessor transparency for model weights? are open-model weights stored in eu?
[12:32] Miguel: weights are hosted in the same region as inference unless model size requires a special host; we can pin model replication to eu-only for your workspace. if you want to use a US-only proprietary model we can treat it as an exception.

[12:55] Leah: small concern — do you do any long-term analytics that aggregate logs across customers in another region?
[13:03] Avery: analytics pipelines are tenancy-aware; aggregated telemetry is anonymised and doesn't include PII. for enterprise we can provide a dedicated analytics pipeline if needed.

[13:20] Miguel: quick note about network egress for EU users: for some payment flows, payment gateway requires us to call US endpoints; those calls can be proxied from your own gateway to maintain egress control.

[13:35] Leah: ok that's helpful. any other compliance artifacts we should ask for?
[13:40] Avery: SOC2, ISO cert, pen test summary, subprocess list, KMS architecture diagram, policy-as-code snippet for routing — we'll send all under NDA.

[13:55] Miguel: last technical question from me: do you want per-tenant subkeys? that is, a unique KMS key per Lockridge subaccount/line-of-business?
[14:05] Sana: yes per-LOB keys would be good, at least for payments.

[14:12] Avery: noted. we'll include per-LOB key options in the architecture doc.

[14:25] Closing recap and next steps below.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 Type II, ISO27001 certificate, and pen-test summary (Avery) - within 2 business days
Redwood to share current subprocessor matrix and mark EU-hosted subprocessors (Miguel) - within 3 business days
Redwood to produce KMS segmentation diagram showing BYOK per-region and proxy flow for private VPC (Miguel) - within 5 business days
Lockridge to provide Okta test credentials and a KMS contact for pilot setup (Sana/Arjun) - by 2027-03-16
Schedule pilot kickoff: 6-week pilot with 1-5% canary traffic for exceptions (schedule via AE)

Miguel: Export and annotate subprocessor CSV with region flags - due 2027-03-12
Miguel: Draft KMS per-region architecture diagram and BYOK flow - due 2027-03-14
Sana/Arjun: Share Okta test account and KMS admin contact - due 2027-03-16
